subject: Availability boundaries for on-prem Redwood deployment
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@tiltcore.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@tiltcore.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: clarify availability commitments for on-prem Redwood Private

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our infra team reviewed the design and we need to make sure the SLA language reflects that TiltCore will manage critical network and power infrastructure on-prem. Specifically, we cannot accept availability credits that assume full control over the underlying facility/network.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide an amendment that (a) distinguishes Redwood-controlled components from TiltCore-controlled components; (b) excludes customer-controlled network/power outages from Redwood uptime calculations; and (c) defines an escalation path and evidence requirements for outage investigations? See attached network diagram and a short request doc.

We are on an aggressive procurement timeline; can we get a proposed amendment this week? Procurement contact is procurement@tiltcore.com.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
VP, Infrastructure & Operations
TiltCore Inc.
Attachments: TiltCore_onprem_network_diagram.png, TiltCore_SLA_Request_2026-04-20.pdf
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara@tiltcore.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: clarify availability commitments for on-prem Redwood Private

Sara —

Thanks for the clear ask and the diagram — very helpful. Looping in Mina (Security) and Markus (Legal) to draft appropriate amendment language.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- We’ll propose an "Availability Boundary" clause that explicitly defines Redwood-controlled services (eg. inference runtime, control plane, KV cache, model assets) vs. customer-controlled infrastructure (eg. network, rack power, physical hosts, internal load balancers).
- Exclude customer-controlled outages from Redwood’s uptime SLOs, while preserving response and investigation SLA for Redwood services when evidence indicates Redwood components caused or contributed to the incident.
- Define evidence and runbook items required for eligibility for service credits (logs, packet captures, change windows).

Draft suggestion (high level):
• "Availability Boundaries: Redwood’s Service Level Objectives apply to Redwood-managed software and services. Outages caused solely by Customer-managed infrastructure (including but not limited to facility power, on-prem network segmentation failures, physical host failure managed by Customer) shall be excluded from Redwood’s uptime calculations."

I’ll come back with redlined language and suggested proof requirements by end of day Wednesday. If TiltCore procurement needs a non-standard term approval, please loop in your procurement contact and we’ll flag for a legal review.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Sara / Jonas —

Thanks — see proposed amendment language below. I tried to balance customer needs with reasonable proof and remediation limits.

--- Proposed Amendment (redwood suggested) ---
1) Definitions
  a) "Redwood-Controlled Components": the Redwood inference runtime, control plane endpoints, model artifacts, logging and tracing services, and any Redwood-delivered software components installed as part of Redwood Private.
  b) "Customer-Controlled Components": physical hosts, rack-level power, on-prem network fabric, Customer-managed load balancers, and any Customer-run middleware outside Redwood-delivered components.

2) Availability Boundary
  Redwood’s uptime SLOs shall not apply to downtime attributable solely to Customer-Controlled Components. Where both Redwood-Controlled Components and Customer-Controlled Components contribute to an incident, Redwood’s uptime calculation shall be adjusted to exclude periods caused exclusively by Customer-Controlled Components, provided Customer supplies required evidence (see Section 4).

3) Evidence & Investigation
  a) To request credit or adjustment, Customer must provide: relevant Redwood logs (as reasonably available), network device logs, change window records, and any relevant BMC/outage tickets.
  b) Redwood will perform a joint investigation within the agreed incident SLA window and will provide a written determination within 10 business days of receiving Customer evidence.

4) Remedies & Limits
  a) Service credits for adjusted downtime shall be pro-rated based on verified Redwood impact but shall remain capped at 25% of the monthly service fee for the affected service.
  b) No credits will be issued where Customer fails to provide requested evidence within 15 business days of Redwood’s request.

5) Operational Readiness
  Customer agrees to provide network topology, maintenance windows, and at least one on-call contact for incident triage. Redwood agrees to provide runbook integration guidance and a list of Redwood monitoring outputs that can be shared for joint troubleshooting.

--- end proposed amendment ---

Jonas — if TiltCore is comfortable with this, we’ll prepare a formal amendment (redline against the Master Services Agreement) and route through procurement.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Folks —

From a security and compliance perspective, two quick items to include in the amendment or an associated appendix:

1) Control plane & audit logs: Redwood will retain control-plane audit logs and provide time-limited read access for incident investigations while ensuring keys remain under Redwood’s KMS policies. We should explicitly state which logs Redwood will provide and the retention window (suggest 90 days default, configurable).

2) Access & Escalation: define a joint incident response playbook with named contacts and an SLA for Redwood to acknowledge and open a joint incident within 1 hour of a suspected Redwood-service impact. Also require that any packet captures or deep network evidence provided by Customer be sanitized for PII before being shared.

Markus — consider adding the audit log and playbook bullets to the Operational Readiness section.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
